profile.personalityShadowSubtitle: Capabilities you have, but haven't been treating as assets
profile.shadowConceptCardBody1: The shadow isn't a flaw. It's the side of you that's there — but you rarely activate.
profile.shadowConceptCardBody2: Some of your capabilities got labeled as 'too much' or 'not enough' by the cultures around you, so you stopped counting them as strengths.
profile.shadowConceptCardBody3: The {{count}} dimension(s) below are what the algorithm found in your data — capabilities you have, but haven't been using as assets. Each one shows: what it is, how you know it's you, and how to use it.
profile.valueConflictExplanation: These values pull against each other in certain decisions. This isn't a problem to solve — it's a tension to manage over time.
profile.boundaryArchetypeExplanation: Your primary and secondary dimensions are very close in score, which means the same you can show up differently across contexts — sometimes {{archetypeLabel}}, sometimes a different mode altogether. This isn't instability. It's context-sensitivity. Recognizing which mode is leading right now lets you choose, instead of being pulled around by the environment.
profile.shadowFootnote: What you've been calling 'too much' or 'not enough' might be a capability that's been waiting for the right context. Seeing it is already a step toward using it.

profile.tipCoreQualities: Your core qualities reveal what makes you uniquely valuable — and where overuse can become a blind spot
profile.coreQualitiesNote: Based on Ofman's Core Qualities model (2004). Your strongest traits, taken too far, become pitfalls. Your growth edge is the positive opposite of that pitfall.
profile.tipSocialStyle: Your social style shapes how others experience you — and how they prefer to communicate with you
profile.socialStyleNote: Based on Kramlinger's Social Styles model (2011). Derived from your personality dimensions.
profile.tipLeadership: Understanding your natural leadership style helps you adapt to different team situations
profile.leadershipStyleNote: Based on Goleman's 6 Leadership Styles (2000). Effective leaders flex across styles based on context.
profile.cardInterpersonalEnergySummary: How you show up in social spaces
profile.tipInterpersonalEnergy: Your interpersonal energy reveals how you naturally engage with people — not better or worse, just your rhythm
profile.interpersonalEnergyNote: Based on the Interpersonal Circumplex model (Wiggins 1979, Locke 2023). Derived from your personality facets.
profile.ieAgencyDesc: Drive to lead, assert, and influence
profile.ieCommunionDesc: Drive to connect, support, and empathize
profile.ieQuadrantDesc_assured-warm: You naturally take charge while making people feel included. Others see you as a confident connector.
profile.ieQuadrantDesc_assured-reserved: You lead with quiet conviction. Others respect your independence and directness.
profile.ieQuadrantDesc_unassuming-warm: You create safety for others. Your support is genuine and your patience is a strength.
profile.ieQuadrantDesc_unassuming-reserved: You observe before you engage. Your reflective nature brings depth to interactions.
profile.ieModeDesc_amplifier: You gain energy from group interaction. Social settings charge your battery.
profile.ieModeDesc_curator: You're selective about social investment. Quality connections over quantity.
profile.ieModeDesc_observer: You recharge in solitude. Deep focus is your superpower.
profile.tipConflictHandling: There's no single 'right' conflict style — each has its place. Knowing yours helps you flex intentionally
profile.conflictHandlingNote: Based on the Thomas-Kilmann Conflict Mode Instrument (1974). Validated mapping from Big Five facets (Dijkstra et al. 2023).
profile.chAssertDesc: How strongly you pursue your own concerns
profile.chCoopDesc: How strongly you pursue others' concerns
profile.chModeDesc_competing: You stand firm on your position. Useful when quick, decisive action is needed.
profile.chModeDesc_collaborating: You seek win-win solutions. Ideal when both parties' concerns are too important to compromise.
profile.chModeDesc_compromising: You find practical middle ground. Effective when time pressure demands a workable solution.
profile.chModeDesc_avoiding: You step back from confrontation. Strategic when the issue is trivial or emotions need to cool.
profile.chModeDesc_accommodating: You prioritize the relationship. Valuable when harmony matters more than the outcome.
profile.cardInterpersonalSummary: How you connect, communicate, and navigate relationships
profile.tipInterpersonal: These insights reveal your relational patterns — how others experience you, and where you can grow in relationships
profile.interpersonalInsufficientData: More data needed to generate interpersonal insights.
profile.interpersonalNote: Derived from your personality facets and behavioral scenarios. These are tendencies, not fixed traits.

profile.frontispieceEmpty: A self still being written. It was never meant to end.
profile.tensionTabSubtitle: Where your dimensions pull in different directions
profile.tensionPageIntro: This page answers one question: where do you get stuck, and why? These aren't weaknesses — they're creative tensions that reveal your deeper priorities.
profile.tensionSjtWhatDesc: How closely your actual behavioral instincts match what you believe you should do
profile.tensionSjtHigh: Your actions closely match your ideals. This self-alignment is rare — but it can also mean your comfort zone is well-guarded.
profile.tensionSjtMedium: Some gaps between your ideals and instincts — these gaps are where your real priorities show through, not your stated ones.
profile.tensionSjtLow: Notable gap between what you think you should do and what you'd actually do. This doesn't mean you lack integrity — it means some situations bypass your conscious values and trigger deeper instincts.
profile.tensionFacetSubtitle: Opposing traits within the same dimension — these create depth, not contradiction
profile.tensionFacetWhatDesc: Within a single personality dimension, you score high on one sub-trait and low on another. This isn't inconsistency — it's complexity.
profile.tensionValueWhatDesc: Two values you genuinely hold pull in opposite directions. When you have to choose between them, you feel an inner tug-of-war.
profile.tensionCrossSubtitle: Where your interests, personality, and values point in different directions
profile.tensionCrossWhatDesc: Different frameworks give contradictory signals — your interests say one thing, your personality another. This is often the root of career confusion.
profile.tensionEmptyDesc: Good news — no major inner conflicts detected. This means your interests, personality, and values are pulling in roughly the same direction, which makes career decisions clearer for you.
profile.tensionEmptyExplainSjt: Say vs. Do gaps — differences between your ideals and actual behavior patterns
profile.tensionEmptyExplainFacet: Personality contradictions — e.g., high discipline but also high impulsiveness within the same trait
profile.tensionEmptyExplainValues: Value conflicts — when two core values you hold pull in opposite directions
profile.tensionEmptyExplainCross: Cross-framework tensions — where your interests, personality, and values don't align
profile.tensionEmptyWhyGood: Not seeing tensions is a genuine strength. But if career decisions ever feel harder than expected, a coaching session can help surface what the numbers don't catch.

dataUsagePoints: Your assessment answers are used solely to generate your career profile and reports.
AI coaching conversations are stored to maintain context within your sessions.
Your data is never sold, shared with third parties, or used for advertising.
Your data is protected by industry-standard security measures.
You can export or delete all your data at any time from this page.
privacy.overviewDesc: Your data is stored securely and used only to generate your career insights.
privacy.personalizationDesc: Allow AI to use your assessment data for personalized coaching and recommendations.
privacy.conversationSavingDesc: Store coaching conversations to maintain context across sessions.
privacy.thirdPartyDesc: Deep Dive does not share your personal data with any third parties. Your data stays with you.
privacy.privacyFaq1A: Your data is stored in secure cloud databases with industry-standard security protections.
privacy.privacyFaq2Q: Can I use Deep Dive without saving data?
privacy.privacyFaq2A: Quick Dive works without an account. Deep Dive assessments require an account to save your results, but you can delete all data at any time.
privacy.privacyFaq3Q: What happens when I delete my data?
privacy.privacyFaq3A: After requesting deletion, there is a 30-day cooling period. After that, all your data is permanently and irreversibly removed from our systems.
